excerpts: New data reveals wholesale eSIM pricing updates in sudden batches, challenging standard ten-minute quote validity windows for AI agents.

Developers building infrastructure for AI agents often assume wholesale prices drift smoothly. A new analysis from the team behind the eSIM operator kit proves otherwise. By comparing nightly catalogue backups from October 19 to November 18, 2026, they discovered that prices remain static for long stretches before jumping in sudden, synchronized batches. The investigation began when an engineer from APIbase questioned the validity of a ten-minute quote window used in the kit. The team admitted the duration was arbitrary. To find the real answer, they analyzed 18 nightly archives of the eSIM Access catalogue, containing between 1,725 and 1,823 plans. The data showed 402 price changes across 377 plans in 30 days, but these were not distributed evenly.

For the first 17 days of the observation period, no prices changed. Then, the behavior shifted dramatically. In the following 13 daily intervals, seven days brought batches of 16 to 111 price changes, while six days remained completely static. The majority of these changes were price cuts, with a median drop of 14.3%. However, all 46 price increases occurred in a single update window between November 15 and 16, with a median rise of 25.2% and a maximum spike of 88.2%. To pinpoint the timing, the team deployed a recorder on November 18 that checked the catalogue every five minutes. They observed a batch of 17 plan cuts landing between the 16:14 and 16:30 UTC reads. This confirmed that the risk for a developer is not slow drift, but a wholesale price update landing inside a short quote validity window. While the probability of a single quote overlapping a batch is low, roughly 0.4%, it affects all plans in that batch simultaneously.
Current data covers only one supplier, eSIM Access, and represents catalogue costs rather than actual transaction prices, requiring further observation for broader applicability.
